in_context.text: After warning Gaius about Diotrephes and urging him to follow what is good, the elder commends a man named Demetrius. Everyone speaks well of him, the truth itself backs him up, and the elder adds his own witness. Gaius can trust that witness.

speaker.text: "The elder," the unnamed writer of the letter. Early Christian tradition identifies him as John the apostle. Some scholars think he was a different church leader.

audience.text: Gaius, a believer the elder loves and counts among his children in the faith.

affected.text: Demetrius, a Christian disciple named only here. He is a different man from the silversmith Demetrius in Acts 19.

what.text: The elder gives Demetrius a threefold recommendation: a good report from all, the witness of the truth itself, and the elder's own record. He then reminds Gaius that his record is true.

events.text: Written while travelling Christian workers depended on churches to house them and send them on. Diotrephes was turning such visitors away.

written.text: Traditional view: about AD 85-95, around the time of 1 and 2 John. Scholarly view: most scholars also place it in the late first century.

where.text: The letter does not say where it was written. Early tradition places John's last years in Ephesus. It went to a church where Gaius lived, likely in the province of Asia.

purpose.text: After the bad example of Diotrephes, the elder points Gaius to a good one. Verse 11 says "he that doeth good is of God," and Demetrius is shown to be such a person.

big_picture.text: The letter values walking in the truth. Here a person's life is said to be confirmed by "the truth itself." Other Scripture also uses "good report" for trustworthy people, such as Ananias and Cornelius, and asks it of church leaders.

for_readers.text: A trustworthy Christian is known by a consistent life that others can witness to and that matches the truth. This is also how believers should walk before outsiders.

key_words.english: hath good report (witness has been given)

why_it_matters.text: The word means to be a witness or to testify. So Demetrius's "good report" is testimony borne about him, not just a passing reputation.
The word can mean the reality of a matter, and also sincerity and integrity of character. The same word appears in 3 John 1:3. Here "the truth itself" stands as a witness alongside people.
The word means witness, testimony or evidence. The lexicon lists it in John 19:35 and 21:24, where the same kind of claim is made that the testimony is true.
Used of things, it means true and conforming to reality. The lexicon lists it with John 19:35 and 21:24, which use the same wording about trustworthy witness.

takeaway.text: Demetrius is commended by everyone, by the truth, and by the elder. He stands as a living example of the good that Gaius should follow, in contrast to Diotrephes.
